file_io.label: File I/O
file_io.description: Reads or writes a file, or manipulates file handles/paths.

network_io.label: Network I/O
network_io.description: Opens a socket/connection, sends/receives over a network, or makes an HTTP request.

process_exec.label: Process / command execution
process_exec.description: Spawns another process or executes a shell command.

memory_management.label: Manual memory management
memory_management.description: Explicit allocation/deallocation - mainly relevant to C/C++; other listed languages are usually garbage-collected, so an empty list there is expected, not a gap.

env_config_access.label: Environment / configuration access
env_config_access.description: Reads process environment variables, configuration, or process/host identity.

logging_output.label: Logging / console output
logging_output.description: Writes diagnostic or user-facing text output. (fprintf is deliberately categorized under file_io instead, since it targets an arbitrary FILE* - avoids the same name winning two categories.)

crypto_security.label: Cryptography / security-sensitive operation
crypto_security.description: Hashing, encryption, random-number generation for security purposes, or credential handling.

string_formatting.label: String formatting / parsing
string_formatting.description: Formats, tokenizes, or parses strings (a heavy hitter in CLI tools that build human-readable output).

low_level_hardware.label: Low-level hardware / privileged operation
low_level_hardware.description: Direct hardware access: port I/O, MSR/control-register access, cache/ TLB/barrier management, and syscall traps executed via *embedded assembly* rather than a libc wrapper. Populated two ways: (1) taught call-names for wrapper functions/macros confirmed by inspection to wrap such an operation (e.g. `outb`, `rdmsr` helper macros - the bottom-up "confirm once, reuse top-down" flow via `add_behavior_signature`), and (2) structurally, at scan time, from `structural_signals.inline_assembly` node hits whose mnemonics match `assembly_instruction_sets` below - see scan_c_behavior.

nonlocal_control_flow.label: Non-local control transfer / coroutine-style context switch
nonlocal_control_flow.description: Jumps out of normal call/return flow (setjmp/longjmp) or swaps an entire execution context (ucontext) - the C-level building block underneath many userspace coroutine/fiber libraries.

concurrency.label: Threading / locking / synchronization
concurrency.description: Creates or synchronizes concurrent execution: POSIX threads, semaphores, OpenMP runtime calls, and Linux kernel locking primitives (spinlocks/mutexes/RCU) share this category since they all answer the same question - "is this coordinating concurrent access?". OpenMP `#pragma omp` regions are detected structurally too (see structural_signals.openmp_pragma), since most parallel loops carry no omp_* call at all.

ipc.label: Inter-process communication
ipc.description: System V and POSIX IPC: shared memory, message queues, and named pipes/semaphores used to communicate BETWEEN processes (as opposed to concurrency's within-process/thread synchronization).

distributed_parallel.label: Distributed / message-passing parallelism (MPI)
distributed_parallel.description: MPI (MPICH/Open MPI) calls - parallelism across separate processes/nodes via explicit message passing, distinct from shared-memory concurrency.

arbitrary_precision_math.label: Arbitrary-precision arithmetic (GMP)
arbitrary_precision_math.description: GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library - bignum integer/rational/float math used by crypto and numerical code needing more than native register width.

time_date.label: Time / date
time_date.description: Reads or manipulates wall-clock time, monotonic clocks, or calendar date/time.

user_kernel_boundary.label: Linux kernel user/kernel memory boundary crossing
user_kernel_boundary.description: THE canonical taint boundary inside Linux kernel code: copy_from_user/get_user bring untrusted userspace data INTO the kernel (a source); copy_to_user/put_user send kernel data OUT to userspace (a sink - an info-leak if the wrong buffer reaches it). Deliberately its own category rather than folded into file_io/memory_management, because THIS boundary is the one that actually matters for kernel security auditing - wired into tools.dataflow_tools as both a SOURCE and a SINK category.

kernel_module_lifecycle.label: Linux kernel module / driver lifecycle
kernel_module_lifecycle.description: Module init/exit, interrupt registration, and character/platform-device driver registration - the scaffolding around a kernel module's entry points.

uefi_service.label: UEFI Boot/Runtime Services (EDK2)
uefi_service.description: EDK2/UEFI protocol-based services, called either directly (MdePkg library wrappers like AllocatePool) or through the global gBS/gRT tables (gBS->LocateProtocol becomes callee name `LocateProtocol` under this project's field-expression approximation - see tools.behavior_tools._c_call_name). NOTE: CreateEvent is claimed here rather than in winapi_platform - both UEFI and Win32 define a function with this exact name, an unavoidable collision under a flat name->category lookup; this project is UEFI/BIOS-focused, so UEFI wins the bare name and Win32's is listed as CreateEventA/CreateEventW instead.

winapi_platform.label: Windows API (Win32)
winapi_platform.description: Windows platform API surface - file/handle, process/thread, registry, and memory management. See uefi_service's note about the CreateEvent name collision.

graphics_rendering.label: GPU / graphics rendering (OpenGL)
graphics_rendering.description: OpenGL (and GLU/GLFW-adjacent) calls - draw commands, buffer/texture/shader object management.

simd_vector.label: SIMD / vector intrinsics
simd_vector.description: Compiler intrinsic functions for explicit vector/SIMD operations (as opposed to auto-vectorization, which is invisible at the source level) - x86 SSE/AVX (immintrin.h) and ARM NEON (arm_neon.h) intrinsic names. Raw SIMD ASSEMBLY mnemonics (for inline-asm blocks) are matched separately via assembly_instruction_sets's per-arch `simd_vector` bucket, since those never appear as a call_expression.

gpu_compute.label: GPU compute / explicit device-resource APIs (CUDA, OpenCL, Vulkan)
gpu_compute.description: Explicit GPU resource and command-queue management - device/context creation, buffer allocation, kernel launch/dispatch. Kept separate from graphics_rendering (OpenGL's immediate-mode-ish draw calls): CUDA/OpenCL/Vulkan all share the same "manage device, buffer, queue, command, then submit" shape even though Vulkan also renders. Intel oneAPI/SYCL is intentionally NOT padded with guessed names here - it's a header-only C++ template API (sycl::queue, sycl::buffer, parallel_for as methods/lambdas), not free functions, so it isn't reliably caught by this project's call-name matching; that gap is honest, not an oversight.

linear_algebra.label: Linear algebra (BLAS / cuBLAS / cuDNN)
linear_algebra.description: Dense matrix/vector math (BLAS + CBLAS wrapper names) and its GPU equivalents - cuBLAS (matrix ops) and cuDNN (neural-net primitives: convolution/pooling/activation).

multimedia_io.label: Desktop multimedia (SDL2: window/renderer/audio/image)
multimedia_io.description: SDL2 core (window/renderer/event loop) plus its companion libraries SDL_image and SDL_mixer (image loading, audio/music playback).

gui_toolkit.label: Desktop GUI toolkit
gui_toolkit.description: Widget-toolkit calls (window/button/label/layout construction, event listeners) - kept separate from multimedia_io since a widget toolkit is a different concern from raw window/audio/image primitives. Started as C/GTK3+GDK only; Java's Swing/AWT/SWT are the same behavior concept in a different language, not a new category.

shader_language.label: Shader built-ins (GLSL / HLSL)
shader_language.description: Built-in functions from GLSL (OpenGL/Vulkan shading language) and HLSL (DirectX shading language) - most names are shared/near- identical between the two (normalize, dot, cross, clamp, mix/lerp, length, reflect, refract, pow, texture sampling). HONEST GAP #1: nothing currently PARSES .glsl/.hlsl/.vert/.frag source - there is no tree-sitter grammar for either wired into tools.behavior_tools, and shader code embedded as a C string literal is invisible to the C AST (a string is just a string to tree-sitter-c). HONEST GAP #2 (why these are NOT under `languages.c` like every other category): almost every one of these names (pow, clamp, length, distance, mix, dot, mul) is also a completely ordinary, extremely common C/C++ identifier unrelated to shaders (`pow` is literally libc's math.h function) - putting them in the real "c" lookup that scan_c_behavior uses would mislabel ordinary math/utility code as shader code. Deliberately filed under a separate `glsl_hlsl` language key instead, inert until a real GLSL/HLSL-aware scanner exists to use it correctly.

gpio_io.label: GPIO line control (libgpiod)
gpio_io.description: Userspace GPIO access via the modern libgpiod character-device API (the legacy /sys/class/gpio sysfs interface is just plain file_io - open/write on a path, no dedicated function names to catch).

i2c_bus.label: I2C / SMBus
i2c_bus.description: Linux i2c-dev/SMBus transactions - the standard way userspace (including BMC firmware) talks to sensors, EEPROMs, and other I2C peripherals. The ioctl(fd, I2C_SLAVE, addr) address-set step itself just shows up as the generic `ioctl` name under file_io.

peci_bus.label: PECI (Platform Environment Control Interface)
peci_bus.description: Intel PECI - the sideband bus a BMC uses to query CPU temperature/config registers directly, without going through the host OS. Directly relevant to this project's BMC/IPMI domain (ipmitool's sensor-reading code is PECI's userspace-visible sibling).

kernel_mailbox.label: Linux kernel mailbox framework (BMC<->host IPC)
kernel_mailbox.description: The kernel mailbox subsystem used for BMC<->host or SoC<->coprocessor message passing (e.g. ASPEED/Nuvoton BMC mailbox controllers) - a hardware-backed IPC channel, distinct from the OS-level `ipc` category.

usb_hid.label: USB / HID device access (libusb, hidapi, WinUSB)
usb_hid.description: Cross-platform USB bulk/control/interrupt transfers and HID report I/O - libusb + hidapi on Linux, WinUSB + the hid.dll HidD_* API + SetupAPI device enumeration on Windows. Kept as one category since it's the same conceptual operation (talk to a USB device) regardless of OS.

device_tree_api.label: Linux kernel Device Tree (OF) runtime API
device_tree_api.description: The kernel-side counterpart to the static .dts/.dtsi descriptions build_system_tools.py now recognizes (device_tree_source) - drivers call this API to read properties/resources out of the device tree the bootloader handed the kernel.

structured_data_parsing.label: Structured document parsing (libxml2 / cJSON)
structured_data_parsing.description: XML (libxml2) and JSON (cJSON) parsing/building - config-file and IPC-payload handling common in both embedded Linux and UEFI tooling.

archive_compression.label: Archive / compression
archive_compression.description: Packs, unpacks, or compresses files - a heavy hitter in build/deploy/install scripts across all three shells.

process_monitoring.label: Process / session monitoring and job control
process_monitoring.description: Inspects or controls ALREADY-RUNNING processes/jobs/sessions - distinct from process_exec (which SPAWNS a new process). ps/top/lsof read process state; jobs/bg/fg/wait are shell job control; tmux/who/whoami are session-level.

network_admin.label: Network interface / firewall administration
network_admin.description: Configures or inspects network interfaces and packet-filtering rules - distinct from network_io (which SENDS/RECEIVES data over the network already-configured interfaces provide).

filesystem_management.label: Filesystem mount / space management
filesystem_management.description: Mounts/unmounts filesystems, checks/repairs them, or reports disk usage - distinct from file_io (which reads/writes INSIDE an already-mounted filesystem).

version_control.label: Version control
version_control.description: Source-control operations invoked from a script (very common in build/deploy/CI tooling).

kernel_proc_sysfs.label: Linux /proc and /sys introspection
kernel_proc_sysfs.description: Reading process/kernel state via the procfs (/proc) and sysfs (/sys) pseudo-filesystems - populated primarily via well_known_paths matching an open()/fopen() call's path argument (see tools.behavior_tools._detect_well_known_paths), since 'open a file' gives no category signal on its own.

arithmetic_logic.label: Arithmetic / logic / compare (ALU operations)
arithmetic_logic.description: Register-level arithmetic (add/sub/mul/div), bitwise logic (and/or/xor/shift), and comparison/flag-setting instructions - the actual computational core of a function, as opposed to control flow (branches) or data movement (load/store). Populated only via assembly_instruction_sets (no C/Java/... call-name equivalent - arithmetic in source languages is an OPERATOR, not a function call).

reflection_metaprogramming.label: Reflection / metaprogramming
reflection_metaprogramming.description: Inspects or invokes code by NAME at runtime rather than through a normal static call site (Class.forName + Method.invoke, Python's getattr/setattr, JS's Reflect/Proxy) - a real behavior worth flagging on its own, since it makes ordinary static call-graph analysis (tools.callgraph_tools) incomplete by construction: a reflectively-invoked method has NO call_expression/method_invocation edge to it at all, and this category cannot fix that gap, only flag where it might exist.

osgi_module_system.label: OSGi bundle lifecycle / service registry
osgi_module_system.description: OSGi's module system - bundle start/stop lifecycle and the dynamic service registry (register/lookup/unregister a service by interface) - the Java-ecosystem analogue of kernel_module_lifecycle's load/unload/register-driver shape, for a completely different runtime.

database_access.label: Database access (SQL / JDBC)
database_access.description: Opens a database connection, prepares/executes a SQL statement, or reads a result set - kept separate from generic file_io since a SQL injection/connection-leak finding is a distinct concern from a plain file read/write.

dom_manipulation.label: DOM query / creation / mutation
dom_manipulation.description: Reads or changes the browser's live document tree - queries an element by id/selector, creates/appends/removes a node, or reads/writes an attribute or class list. Kept separate from gui_toolkit (a DESKTOP widget-toolkit concept - window/button/layout construction) since the DOM is the browser's native document model, not a widget toolkit, and separate from event_handling (listening for/reacting to events is a different concern from shaping the tree itself). Honest trade-off: several entries here (`appendChild`, `remove`, `closest`, `matches`) are bare DOM method names with no receiver qualification - a class that happens to define its OWN method of the same name (e.g. a custom `remove()`) would be misclassified the same way any bare-name category entry can be, in any language; not attempting per-receiver-type resolution (not statically knowable without a type system) is a documented scope limit, not an oversight.

event_handling.label: Event listener registration / dispatch
event_handling.description: Registers, removes, or manually fires a DOM/browser event, or intercepts its default behavior/propagation - a distinct concern from dom_manipulation (shaping the tree) and from asynchronous control flow (concurrency category's Promise/timer entries), since "does this function react to something happening" is its own real behavior question.

browser_storage.label: Browser client-side storage (localStorage / sessionStorage / IndexedDB)
browser_storage.description: Persists or reads data in the browser itself (not a server round-trip, not a filesystem call) - localStorage/sessionStorage's synchronous key-value API and IndexedDB's async transactional object-store API. Kept separate from file_io (server/OS-level file access) since a browser storage leak/quota concern is a distinct issue from a filesystem one. IndexedDB entries follow this taxonomy''s existing convention-based-receiver-name approach (same trade-off as database_access''s `cursor.execute`/`pool.query` - IndexedDB has no fixed global object name to hang a call on, only conventional local variable names like `db`/`store`).

browser_dialog.label: Native browser modal dialog
browser_dialog.description: Pops a blocking, native (non-DOM, non-stylable) browser dialog - alert/confirm/prompt - kept separate from dom_manipulation/logging_output since a blocking modal that halts script execution until the user responds is a distinct UX/behavior concern from either passively writing to the tree or the console.

x86.name: memset_zero_or_fill
x86.template: clears/fills a block of memory one BYTE at a time (the classic `rep stosb` bzero/memset idiom - AL holds the fill value, ECX/RCX the byte count, EDI the destination)

x86.name: memset_zero_or_fill
x86.template: clears/fills a block of memory one WORD (2 bytes) at a time (`rep stosw`)

x86.name: memset_zero_or_fill
x86.template: clears/fills a block of memory one DOUBLEWORD (4 bytes) at a time (`rep stosd`)

x86.name: memset_zero_or_fill
x86.template: clears/fills a block of memory one QUADWORD (8 bytes) at a time, 64-bit mode (`rep stosq`)

x86.name: memcpy
x86.template: copies a block of memory one BYTE at a time (the classic `rep movsb` memcpy idiom - ECX/RCX the byte count, ESI the source, EDI the destination)

x86.name: memcpy
x86.template: copies a block of memory one WORD (2 bytes) at a time (`rep movsw`)

x86.name: memcpy
x86.template: copies a block of memory one DOUBLEWORD (4 bytes) at a time (`rep movsd`)

x86.name: memcpy
x86.template: copies a block of memory one QUADWORD (8 bytes) at a time, 64-bit mode (`rep movsq`)

x86.name: memcmp
x86.template: compares two blocks of memory byte-by-byte WHILE they keep matching, stopping at the first difference (the classic `repe cmpsb` memcmp idiom)

x86.name: memcmp
x86.template: compares two blocks of memory byte-by-byte WHILE they keep matching, stopping at the first difference (`repz cmpsb`, alias of REPE)

x86.name: memchr_or_strlen
x86.template: scans a block of memory byte-by-byte for a matching value, stopping at the FIRST match (the classic `repne scasb` memchr/strlen-style idiom)

x86.name: memchr_or_strlen
x86.template: scans a block of memory byte-by-byte for a matching value, stopping at the FIRST match (`repnz scasb`, alias of REPNE)
